items.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 12 at 5:00PM EST until November 12 at 8:00PM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ
items.areaDesc: Burlington, NJ; Mercer, NJ; Monmouth, NJ; Bucks, PA
items.description:
At 500 PM EST, flash flooding was reported on US-1 Southbound near
Morrisville in Bucks County.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Trenton, Ewing, Bordentown, Allentown, Crosswicks,
Mercerville-Hamilton Square, Edinburg, Windsor, White Horse,
Georgetown, Imlaystown and Cream Ridge.
items.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 12 at 2:10PM EST until November 13 at 1:00PM EST by NWS State College PA
items.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations up to two inches.
Locally higher amounts up to 4 inches are possible. Winds gusting
as high as 35 mph.

* WHERE...Northern Lycoming, Potter, Sullivan, and Tioga Counties.

* WHEN...From 7 PM this evening to 1 PM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Be prepared for winter driving conditions overnight
through the Friday morning commute.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Rain will change to wet snow tonight and
continue into Friday morning. Snowfall will be elevation dependent
with accumulation most likely above 1500 feet. Snow is most likely
to accumulate on non-paved surfaces. The first snow of the season
can result in greater impacts as motorists adjust to winter driving
conditions.
items.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. Visit www.511pa.com for
the latest travel, roadways, and traffic conditions.

items.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 12 at 7:01PM EST until November 12 at 9:00PM EST by NWS Upton NY
items.areaDesc: Bergen, NJ; Essex, NJ; Hudson, NJ; Passaic, NJ; Union, NJ; Bronx, NY; Kings, NY; Nassau, NY; New York, NY; Queens, NY; Richmond, NY; Westchester, NY
items.description:
* WHAT...Minor flooding caused by heavy rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Bergen County in northeastern New Jersey...
Essex County in northeastern New Jersey...
Hudson County in northeastern New Jersey...
Eastern Passaic County in northeastern New Jersey...
Central Union County in northeastern New Jersey...
Bronx County in southeastern New York...
Kings (Brooklyn) County in southeastern New York...
Nassau County in southeastern New York...
New York (Manhattan) County in southeastern New York...
Queens County in southeastern New York...
Richmond (Staten Island) County in southeastern New York...
Southern Westchester County in southeastern New York...

* WHEN...Until 900 PM EST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 700 PM EST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has
fallen in the last few hours.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Newark, Jersey City, Jamaica, Yonkers, Paterson, Elizabeth,
Flatbush, New Rochelle, Flushing, Passaic, Bayonne, Wayne, Mott
Haven, Hoboken and Bloomfield.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

items.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 12 at 6:26PM EST until November 12 at 10:00PM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ
items.description:
At 626 PM EST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 0.5 to 1 inch in 1 hour.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the warned
area. Flash flooding is already occurring on NJ 35 north of Sylvania
Ave in Neptune City with lanes closed in both directions.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Long Branch, Asbury Park, Tinton Falls, Manasquan, Point Pleasant
Beach, Allenwood, Collingwood Park, Elberon, Ramtown, Point
Pleasant, Eatontown and West Long Branch.
items.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

items.headline: Coastal Flood Statement issued November 12 at 2:08PM EST until November 13 at 6:00PM EST by NWS Boston/Norton MA
items.description:
* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways (3.2 to 11.6 feet Mean Lower Low Water).

* WHERE...Barnstable MA and Nantucket MA Counties.

* WHEN...Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Roads remain passable. Low lying areas and roads
near Nantucket Harbor, including Easy Street, may experience
pockets of shallow flooding less than one foot deep.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Splashover and very minor coastal flooding
are possible during the Friday afternoon high tide along north
facing beaches on Cape Cod Bay as well as Nantucket sound. No
significant impacts are expected and any splashover/very minor
coastal flooding will be quite short-lived, no more than an hour
on either side of high tide.
items.instruction: Do not drive through flooded roadways.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 12 at 12:29PM EST until November 13 at 10:00AM EST by NWS Burlington VT
items.areaDesc: Western Essex; Eastern Addison; Eastern Rutland
items.description:
* WHAT...Wet snow expected mainly above 1200 feet. Total snow
accumulations between 2 and 4 inches.

* WHERE...In New York, Western Essex County. In Vermont, Eastern
Addison and Eastern Rutland Counties.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slippery road conditions. The hazardous
conditions will impact the Thursday evening and Friday morning
commutes. Roads, and especially bridges and overpasses, will likely
become slick and hazardous.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Impacts from snow will begin at higher
elevations today becoming more widespread in the Advisory areas
after 7 PM this evening as snow levels descend.
items.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest on road
conditions in Vermont, visit https://newengland511.org and for New
York, visit https://511ny.org.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 12 at 12:27PM EST until November 13 at 10:00AM EST by NWS Albany NY
items.areaDesc: Hamilton; Northern Warren; Bennington; Western Windham
items.description:
* WHAT...Snow. Total snow accumulations up to 3 inches with isolated
totals of 3 to 5 inches for the highest mountain peaks.

* WHERE...Northern Warren and Hamilton Counties in New York and
elevations above 1500 feet in Bennington and Western Windham
Counties in Vermont.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slippery road conditions.
items.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for the state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Be prepared for slippery roads. Slow down and use caution while
driving. If you are going outside, watch your first few steps taken
on stairs, sidewalks, and driveways. These surfaces could be icy and
slippery, increasing your risk of a fall and injury.
